title: Flood made your Sebastian home unlivable? How Florida's property tax refund works, and the March 1 deadline
seoTitle: Sebastian Flood Damage: Property Tax Refund (DR-465)
description: If this week's flood left your Sebastian home unlivable for 30 days or more, Florida may refund part of your 2026 property tax. Who qualifies and how to apply.
dek: Florida has a little-known refund for homes a disaster makes unlivable. It is not automatic, it has a 30-day rule, and the form goes to the property appraiser's office on U.S. 1 in Sebastian. Here is how it works.
facebook: Did this week's flood push you out of your Sebastian home? Florida law may give back part of your 2026 property tax if the house stays unlivable for 30 days or more. Here's who qualifies, the one form you need, and the March 1 deadline.
keywords: Sebastian flood damage property tax refund
Florida catastrophic event tax refund DR-465
Indian River County property appraiser flood damage
home uninhabitable 30 days property tax refund Florida
report flood damage Indian River County

body.text: Sebastian got hit hard this week. Floodwater closed streets, stalled cars in front of Sebastian Middle School overnight, and shut eastbound County Road 512 between I-95 and County Road 510. Waste Management even stopped pickup on Tuesday because the roads were not safe.

If water got inside your house, you are probably thinking about drywall, floors and where to sleep. Taxes are the last thing on your mind. But Florida has a property tax refund made for exactly this kind of week, and it is easy to miss because nobody sends it to you. You have to ask.

body.title: The short version
body.text: If flooding made your home unlivable for at least 30 days, you may get part of your 2026 property tax back. File Form DR-465 with the Indian River County Property Appraiser by March 1, 2027, and pay your 2026 tax bill in full by March 31, 2027.

Florida law (section 197.319 of the state statutes) lets a homeowner get back part of the property tax paid for the year a "catastrophic event" made the home uninhabitable. The Florida Department of Revenue lists flooding as one of those events, along with hurricanes, tornadoes, fires and water damage.

"Uninhabitable" means you lost the use of the house for what it was built for, because of damage or because its structure was compromised. It is not about being uncomfortable. It is about not being able to live there.

items: Homes only. The refund covers residential property, not commercial buildings.
The house must be unlivable for at least 30 days because of the event.
It covers the house itself, not the land. Detached garages, carports, fences, pools and seawalls do not count.
The refund goes to whoever paid the tax.
You get one refund per event. If the home is still unlivable next year, you cannot claim the same flood again.

body.text: How much money are we talking about?
It is a partial refund, and the math has three parts: how much of your property's value the damaged house represents, how many days it was unlivable out of 365, and how much tax you paid.

The Department of Revenue's homeowner guide gives an example. A $300,000 property whose value drops to $75,000 without the house, with 95 days unlivable and $2,250 in taxes, gets a refund of $438.75. Fewer days means a smaller check. The property appraiser decides if you qualify, and the tax collector does the math.

items: Now: keep track of the day you had to stop living in the house, and the day you move back in.
March 1, 2027: last day to file Form DR-465 with the property appraiser for a 2026 event.

March 31, 2027: your 2026 property tax must be paid in full. Taxes are still due even if the home is damaged. The state's FAQ says partial payments and payment plans do not count unless the bill is paid in full by then.
By April 1, 2027: if you qualify, the property appraiser must notify you and the tax collector. The tax collector sends the refund.

body.text: Missed March 1? The state's FAQ says you can still ask the Value Adjustment Board, but only by showing special circumstances. Do not count on that. File early.

You do not have to drive to Vero. The Indian River County Property Appraiser has a Sebastian office at 1921 U.S. Highway 1, phone (772) 226-1133, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The main office is at 1800 27th Street in Vero Beach, (772) 226-1469. Form DR-465 is on the appraiser's Applications and Forms page at ircpa.org.

One more thing to know. Florida values property as of January 1. A CBS12 report quoting the Palm Beach County appraiser explained that this week's damage does not change your 2026 assessment, but damage still unrepaired on January 1, 2027 may affect your 2027 assessment. If your house will still be torn up after New Year's, ask the appraiser's office how that works for you.

items: Take photos and video of every damaged room before anything is torn out or thrown away.
Write down the date you stopped living in the house. Keep a simple log of where you stayed.
Save the paper trail the state says can support your application: utility bills, contractor statements, building permit applications, any certificate of occupancy, and your insurance information.
Report the damage to Indian River County through its self-report damage page (linked below), or call the county at (772) 567-8000.
If you are staying somewhere else, update your mailing address with the property appraiser and tax collector so you do not miss notices.
Once you know the home was unlivable for 30 days or more, fill out DR-465 and take it to the Sebastian office on U.S. 1. Ask them to confirm they received it.
Pay your 2026 tax bill in full by March 31, 2027. The refund depends on it.

body.text: A small trash note while you clean up: Waste Management said Sebastian yard waste pickup is paused through Saturday and returns to its normal schedule the week of Nov. 9. Garbage and bulk pickup were catching up Wednesday through Saturday, starting with Monday and Tuesday routes. Leave your carts at the curb until they are emptied.

faq.q: Can I get a property tax refund if my house flooded in Florida?
faq.a: Possibly. Florida section 197.319 allows a partial refund of the year's property tax if a catastrophic event, including flooding, made the home uninhabitable for at least 30 days. You must apply with Form DR-465.

faq.q: When is the deadline for Form DR-465 in Indian River County?
faq.a: For damage in 2026, file with the Indian River County Property Appraiser by March 1, 2027. Your 2026 property tax must also be paid in full by March 31, 2027.

faq.q: Where do I file DR-465 in Sebastian?
faq.a: At the Indian River County Property Appraiser's Sebastian office, 1921 U.S. Highway 1, (772) 226-1133, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The main office is at 1800 27th Street in Vero Beach.

faq.q: Does the refund cover a flooded pool, fence or detached garage?
faq.a: No. The state guide says the refund is for the house itself. Land and non-essential structures such as detached garages, carports, fences, pools and seawalls do not count.

faq.q: Will flood damage lower my 2026 property assessment?
faq.a: No. Florida values property as of January 1, so 2026 values are already set. Damage still unrepaired on January 1, 2027 may affect your 2027 assessment.
